name: Micromobility Device
description: A motorized transportation device for individual use, typically 20 to 36 inches wide and 50 pounds or less, that operates typically under 15 mph and never faster than 28 mph; the term spans bicycles, electric bicycles and motorized scooters, privately owned or shared. A light electric bike outside the e-bike classes that tops out at 28 mph can fit it.

restrictions.rule: Designed for individual use, typically 20 to 36 inches wide and 50 pounds or less; those figures are typical, not hard limits (Florida Statutes §316.003(41))
Operates typically under 15 mph and can't exceed 28 mph (Florida Statutes §316.003(41))
No limit on motor power (Florida Statutes §316.003(41))
No driver's license, registration or insurance required (Florida Statutes §316.2128)
Has a bicycle rider's rights and duties, and is exempt from the ban on motorized vehicles on sidewalks and bicycle paths (Florida Statutes §316.2128)
A local government may regulate it on streets, highways, sidewalks and sidewalk areas (Florida Statutes §316.2128)
Since July 1, 2025 a local government may set minimum ages by ordinance and require riders to carry government-issued photo ID (Florida Statutes §316.2128, as amended by chapter 2025-149)
Before July 1, 2025 the term covered only app-rented shared-fleet devices capped at 20 mph (chapter 2025-149)
